name: Online shop
when: E-commerce and marketplaces: people browse, compare, buy, and come back for their order.

actors.who: Someone who arrived from search or an ad and has never bought here.
questions: What were they looking for when they arrived, in their own words?
What do they need to know before trusting this shop with a payment?
Which device do they buy on, and do they start on one device and finish on another?
What costs or conditions would make them abandon at checkout (delivery price, delivery date, returns)?
How do they compare products: by price, by a spec, by reviews, by photos?

actors.who: Someone who has bought before and comes back to buy again or to check an order.
questions: Why do they come back: to reorder, to track, to return?
Do they expect to be signed in, and what happens if they are not?
What would they need to see to resolve an order problem without contacting support?

screens.name: Catalogue or category
screens.does: Browses a range and narrows it down.

screens.name: Search results
screens.does: Finds the product they have in mind, or a close alternative.

screens.name: Product page
screens.does: Decides whether this is the right product at the right total price and delivery date.

screens.name: Cart
screens.does: Checks what they are buying and what it will cost in total.

screens.name: Checkout
screens.does: Gives delivery and payment details once and places the order.

screens.name: Order confirmation
screens.does: Knows the order went through and what happens next.

screens.name: Order history
screens.does: Finds an order, sees where it is, and starts a return.

journeys.goal: Find a product and buy it
watch: The total cost, including delivery, is visible before the last step.
Checkout can be finished without creating an account.
Count the form fields in checkout; each must be needed to deliver or to charge.
An error in checkout keeps everything the shopper already typed.

journeys.goal: Narrow a range down to one product
watch: Filters apply without losing scroll position, and say how many results remain.
Going back from a product returns to the same place in the list.
The facts people compare on are in the same place on every product page.

journeys.goal: Find a past order and start a return
watch: The order's current status and expected date are visible without opening a sub-page.
The return starts from the order, not from a help article.
Every step says what happens next and when.

research: What do shoppers in this category need to see before buying (sizes, compatibility, ingredients, warranty)?
Which delivery, payment and return options are expected in this market, and which are legally required?
What do customer reviews of this shop and its competitors complain about most?
What share of traffic is on phones, and where does it come from (search, social, email)?
Which local conventions matter: currency format, address format, phone format, tax shown or not?

sources.name: Baymard Institute — e-commerce UX research
sources.why: Large-sample usability research on product pages, search, cart and checkout.

sources.name: Nielsen Norman Group — 10 usability heuristics
sources.why: The baseline vocabulary for reviewing any screen.

sources.name: Shopify Polaris
sources.why: Commerce patterns and content guidelines from a platform that runs many shops.

sources.name: GOV.UK Design System — patterns
sources.why: Researched patterns for addresses, payment details, errors and confirmation pages.
